pr_title: core: add support for setting CPUAffinity= to special "numa" value
pr_body:
systemd will automatically derive CPU affinity mask from NUMA node mask.

Fixes #13248
pr_comments: Test failures are caused by missing `cut` and `taskset` in the built test image. I must say that not having tools from util-linux and coreutils in the image by default is a bit annoying.
@poettering I've accidentally pushed my WIP patch. Sorry about that, but thanks for the review anyway :)

I've pushed the new version. `ExecContext` is no longer modified, numa code was split-off to `numa-util.c|h`.

@keszybz @poettering PTAL

One more update. I've noticed that CI was failing because `systemctl show -p CPUAffinity` didn't report correct value. Now it should.

However, mapping from "numa" to affinity mask is done by PID1, using the same algorithm that we use when we are starting the service (may not report 100% correct value in all cases if a set of NUMA nodes changes, but that is extremely unlikely so this should be good enough).

I've also added a possibility to set `CPUAffinity=numa` via systemd-run. I transport this special value over dbus as an affinity mask that has one bit set at offset `_SC_NPROCESSORS_CONF` (number of CPUs on the box). This should work OK since this number is bigger than the ID of all CPUs.

issue_context.title: RFE: CPUAffinity=NUMA to simplify unification of CPU and Memory resource contraints
issue_context.body:
From #3097: thanks for adding [NUMAPolicy](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.exec.html#NUMAPolicy=) and [NUMAMask](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.exec.html#NUMAMask=).

A `CPUAffinity=NUMA` would be a useful extension to align `CPUAffinity` to the same node as memory.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The ability to set [NUMAMask](#12764) to constrain (per NUMAPolicy) memory allocated to a node usually has a concurrent thought to constrain CPUAffinity to the same NUMAMask nodes as the memory.

The determination of which CPUs are associated with the same memory nodes used in NUMAMask is left as a fragile exercise to the sysadmin leading to faults especially when one settings is changed without another.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A setting of `CPUAffinity=NUMA` could concisely equate the memory and CPU constraints without the possibility of error.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Manually entering `CPUAffinity=` explicit list of CPUs. - Fragile.

`CPUAffinity=NUMA:{numanode1}, NUMA:{numanode1}`, less fragile, however duplication of the list of nodes in `NUMAMask` and not sure what practical use it is to constrain a service to number of CPUs on one node, but memory from two nodes. There might be a cause - if there is this could still be implemented later.

As a libnuma function the start of this is [numa_node_to_cpus](https://linux.die.net/man/3/numa_node_to_cpus), returning a set of cpus.
comments: @grooverdan makes a lot of sense. Thanks for filling the issue. I plan to work on this in the following weeks.

hmm, wouldn#t it make sense to just do this as default behaviour? i.e. if CPUAffinity= is not specified but NUMAMask= is, then automatically use the numa mask also as CPUAffinity=?

i.e. isn't it more common to set both to the same masks than to separate ones, and thus automatica propagation from numa mask to cpu affinity makes sense, and only if people don't want that they should configure CPUAffinity= explicitly?

that would not only be simpler semantically, but also in code.

I don't know if it is necessarily a good idea to do this by default. 

Also on the code level, NUMAMask= and CPUAffinity= are too different objects. NUMAMask= lists NUMA nodes while CPUAffinity= list CPU indices.

A `CPUAffinity=NUMA` seems a consistent default given `NUMAMask=` is all nodes. I've no objection. As `NUMAMask` hasn't been in a release we're not introducing any incompatibility by changing this default though that may change quick with v243 being in RC.

Regarding two different objects they do have significant coupling at an architectural and practical level. The Linux concepts of NUMA seem much more focused on memory (was cpu binding concepts already implemented?) though the original concept of numa node is the tying of cpu and memory.

This RFE encompasses a pragmatism needed by sysadmins to isolate services at a hardware level.

I find the use case invalid. If the user specifies `NUMAMask=`, it's the kernel scheduler's job to balance tasks so that they converge to the CPUs closest to the used memory (if you don't observe that despite `CONFIG_NUMA_BALANCING`, then it's possibly a bug).

Note that there can be  [CPU-less NUMA nodes](https://marc.info/?l=linux-cgroups&m=156458862929379) making the proposed semantics broken. Furthermore, interpretation of the special value would need to be done by the kernel, otherwise there would be no way to respond to CPU/memory hotplug events.

> I find the use case invalid. If the user specifies `NUMAMask=`, it's the kernel scheduler's job to balance tasks so that they converge to the CPUs closest to the used memory (if you don't observe that despite `CONFIG_NUMA_BALANCING`, then it's possibly a bug).

Not sure what you find invalid on administrator's desire to make sure that service (workload) is running with the desired NUMA/CPUAffinity setting from the very beginning w/o relying on rather untransparent behavior on the kernel side. Moreover, if `CONFIG_NUMA_BALANCING` is disabled then your only option is to configure things manually (since `numad` doesn't seem to be a thing anymore).

The proposed value would lead to false believe that the unit will always run on the specified NUMA nodes' CPUs. I see the point that it is a valid requirement.

However, if the administrator's goal is to confine the unit to a particular node, then neither of these settings would help as they can be overriden by the executing process. If the objective is to minimize access distance, then the kernel is the component that has full information (hotplugging, access patterns) and can facilitate that.

@msekletar  do you have an example configuration for this? I would like to create tmpfs mounts based on the number of available NUMA nodes. 

for example, if I have 8 NUMA nodes, I would like to automatically set up tmpfs mounts with these options here:

```
rw,relatime,size=400G,mpol=prefer:<NUMA NODE>" "tmpfs<NODE ID>" "/FOO/tmpfs<NODE ID>/FOOBAR"
```

How would I do this with your change?

Here is an example of what I would like to generate automatically:

```
# systemctl cat /FOO/tmpfs0/BAR

[Unit]
SourcePath=/etc/fstab
Documentation=man:fstab(5) man:systemd-fstab-generator(8)
Before=local-fs.target

[Mount]
Where=/FOO/tmpfs0/BAR
What=tmpfsBAR0
Type=tmpfs
Options=rw,relatime,size=400G,mpol=prefer:0

# systemctl cat /FOO/tmpfs1/BAR

[Unit]
SourcePath=/etc/fstab
Documentation=man:fstab(5) man:systemd-fstab-generator(8)
Before=local-fs.target

[Mount]
Where=/FOO/tmpfs1/BAR
What=tmpfsBAR1
Type=tmpfs
Options=rw,relatime,size=400G,mpol=prefer:1
```

Also: If the numa node size changes on reboot.. there should be no mount for the invalid NUMA node ID, because this would lead to a system crash.

@shibumi unfortunately I don't have any example for this specific use case. AFAICT, it is not possible to do it with the current functionality. This seems like a job for a generator which could determine number of numa nodes and generate corresponding mount units.

review_comments:
hmm, please no, let's just add an explcit bus property for this. i.e. add CPUAffinityFromNuma as boolean bus property.

i.e. let's have a normalized API. Yes, this means that the unit files on disk and the matching dbus properties are slightly differently set up, but we do that all the time, because one is user facing and the other code facing. For user facing stuff we want the more condensed version, for code facing stuff the normalized version. 

Other cases where we do things like this are for example TasksMax=. In unit files it exists only under this name, but accepts both absolute and relative values (i.e. % values). On the wire this is mapped to two distinct properties. TasksMax is used for the absolute values and TasksMaxScale= for the relative values. 

Hence: user facing props should be close to dbus props, but should be fully normalized in their conceptual behaviour.
hmm, this check is pretty much unnecessary, no? the only caller checks this anyway... And semantically it might even be useful to convert the numa mask to cpu affinity if the bool isn't set...

as a matter of coding style, we generally want functions that initialize all return parameters on success and leave them untouched on failure. This function leaves them uninitialized in two success cases, which we really should avoid... And it it might change it even on failure.

To be honest, I don't know, but it is what kernel expects. It decrements the value of the input parameter that it receives from userspace as a first thing in a syscall handler.

https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/mm/mempolicy.c#L1646

uh, this is puzzling... I don't get it. the kernel seems to systematically underflow if i pass maxnodes = 0, which is supported according to the docs...

That said, I think we should calculate with the accurate value wherever we can, i.e. return bits here rather than bits+1, and then add the one extra immediately when invoking the syscall only, with a comment about it.
(usually we validate input before checking if what we need is actually available... but doesn't matter)
